questions.q: Where are Intelligent Query Processing feedback records (Memory Grant Feedback, CE Feedback, DOP Feedback) persisted?
options: In the Query Store, readable via sys.query_store_plan_feedback
questions.explain: IQP feedback is stored as query feedback in the Query Store and persists across connections and server restarts; the chapter inspects it via sys.query_store_plan_feedback with feature_desc values like MemoryGrantFeedback.

questions.q: What calibration period does the chapter say Microsoft recommends before Azure Defender for SQL behavioral alerts become reliable?
questions.explain: Defender's behavioral model trains on your workload's historical access patterns; Microsoft recommends 14 to 30 days of calibration, and major workload changes require re-establishing the baseline.

questions.q: Which index technology does Azure SQL use for its native VECTOR index (CREATE VECTOR INDEX)?
questions.explain: Azure SQL implements vector indexes with DiskANN, designed for billion-scale vector datasets that do not fit in memory by organizing the graph to minimize disk I/O during traversal.

questions.q: Which T-SQL feature lets you call any REST endpoint (including Azure OpenAI deployments) from inside a stored procedure?
questions.explain: sp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint calls any REST endpoint from T-SQL, enabling in-SQL AI enrichment; the chapter notes each call is one API call per row, so batch aggressively.

questions.q: The chapter warns of an oscillation cycle between IQP feedback (e.g., CE Feedback) and Automatic Plan Correction. What is the recommended intervention?
options: Pin a specific plan with sp_query_store_force_plan, or fix the underlying statistics problem
questions.explain: When CE Feedback drives a plan change that Automatic Plan Correction then reverts as a regression, repeated revert entries signal you to intervene manually — either fixing the statistics problem or pinning a plan via sp_query_store_force_plan.
